faqs.question: How do I obtain the latest product software for Windows or my Mac?
faqs.answer: You can download the latest product driver from the Downloads section of this website.

faqs.question: Can the Epson ink cartridges be refilled or can I use third-party ink cartridges without voiding the warranty?
faqs.answer:
Epson does not recommend refilling or using other brands of ink cartridges.  Epson uses a permanent Micro Piezo print head that has allowed Epson to lead the industry in delivering consistent photo image quality by using variable-sized droplets.  Micro Piezo print head can also use a wider variety of inks, which has allowed Epson to introduce such ink breakthroughs as DURABrite® and Epson UltraChrome® inks that offer greatly improved humidity resistance, smudge resistance, and fade resistance.
Using refilled ink cartridges will not void the product's original warranty; however, if these products cause a failure, the repair of that failure will not be covered under warranty.

faqs.question: I see the message Cannot connect to Internet in Windows 8.1 after I select Driver Update in my product software. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
The
Driver Update
option does not work in Windows 8.1. All other driver options will work correctly.

faqs.question: I brought my product with me to a different country and can't find ink for it. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Some Epson printers and ink cartridges are specific to a regional market and not sold worldwide, although the same printers are sold in the U.S. and Canada. If you have a printer sold in the U.S. or Canada, you may not be able to easily get ink cartridges for it in foreign markets.
Unfortunately, because of customs and tax regulations, the Epson E-Stores in the U.S. and Canada are unable to ship to addresses outside the U.S. and Canada.

faqs.question: I am unable to connect my product to a wireless network. What should I do?
faqs.answer: The printer does not come with built-in wireless features and does not support a wireless (or Ethernet) connection to a network router. Only a direct wired connection to the computer is supported.

faqs.question: My product makes noise after I turn it on or after it has been sitting for a while. What should I do?
faqs.answer: This is normal. It is performing routine maintenance.

faqs.question: Does Epson have a program where I can donate my working electronic equipment?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Epson America, Inc. and
Digitunity
have joined together with the goal of helping those who are facing economic challenges or have a disability to gain access to today's technology. With your donation, you not only help the environment, but you also help change the lives of those who need these products the most.

faqs.question: Does Epson make drivers for Linux?
faqs.answer:
Linux drivers are available for some products. Visit the links below to see the drivers available for your product, as well as information about using an Epson product with Linux.
Note:
Epson does not provide support for Linux drivers.
Linux drivers for Epson products
Linux FAQs for Epson products
(only available in English)
Linux manuals for Epson products
(only available in English)

faqs.question: How can I get a replacement CD for my product?
faqs.answer:
You can download the driver from the Downloads tab for your product.
Note
:
Only the drivers are available for download. Any extra software that came with the product is available only on the CD.
If you wish to obtain a replacement copy of the Software CD (stock permitting), please contact our Driver Fulfillment department at 562-276-4367 (US) or 905-709-3839 (Canada). A charge for shipping and handling plus any applicable taxes may apply.

faqs.question: Printing is slow. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Check the following:
It takes a few moments for PictureMate to process your images before printing them. Note, larger image sizes will take longer to process.
If PictureMate is in a hot or sunny location, move it to a cooler place and try printing again.
If you are printing from a computer, make sure it meets the
System Requirements
.
If you print continuously for 30 minutes, PictureMate may slow down to prevent overheating. Leave the printer power on, but allow it to cool off by not printing for at least 30 minutes.
If you're printing a high-resolution image, you may need more than the minimum requirements listed. You may also need to:
Clear space on your hard drive or run a defragmentation utility.
Close programs that you're not using.
Increase your system's memory (RAM).
For faster printing, try these tips:
Don't print more than 40 pictures at a time.
Photos with borders print faster than borderless photos.
Turn off special features such as color effects and red-eye reduction.
If PictureMate is connected to a USB hub, disconnect any USB devices that you're not using.

faqs.question: Why does the wrong photo print?
faqs.answer:
Check the following:
If your camera supports DPOF, you can pre-select photos so PictureMate knows exactly what to print. See
Printing Camera-Selected DPOF Photos
for more information.
If your camera supports PictBridge, you can connect it to PictureMate and control printing from the camera. See
Printing From a Digital Camera
for details.

faqs.question: Why does it take so long to scroll through my pictures on my product's display?
faqs.answer: The file size of the pictures determines the viewing speed. Scrolling takes longer when you are viewing pictures with larger file sizes.

faqs.question: I installed a photo cartridge, but an error message says that it is not the initial cartridge. What should I do?
faqs.answer: For the first cartridge, you must install the photo cartridge that comes in the box with your PictureMate. If you purchased additional PictureMate 200/300 Series Print Packs, use these photo cartridges only as replacements.

faqs.answer:
The
Driver Update
option does not work in Windows 8.1. All other driver options will work correctly.

faqs.question: How do I replace the photo cartridge?
faqs.answer:
See
Replacing the Photo Cartridge
.

faqs.question: How do I know when the photo cartridge needs to be replaced?
faqs.answer:
Your PictureMate will let you know when the photo cartridge is low or expended. See
Checking Photo Cartridge Status
in the
User's Guide
for more information.

faqs.question: How many photos will I get from my product Print Pack?
faqs.answer:
Epson has packaged the PictureMate Photo Cartridge with a quantity of 4×6 PictureMate Photo Paper, so that purchasing supplies for PictureMate is convenient and affordable. The number of sheets of photo paper in your PictureMate Print Pack is stated on the Print Pack's box. The photo ink cartridge in the Print Pack contains enough ink to allow borderless, color printing of about the stated number of sheets.
Our estimate of the number of photos you can print with a PictureMate Print Pack is based on test printing with a range of 20 different color photos. Actual yields will vary based on images printed, print settings, paper type, frequency of use and temperature. For example, printing many copies of the same photo, or printing many black and white or sepia photos, may result in fewer photos per PictureMate Photo Cartridge. Also, the PictureMate Photo Cartridge once installed should be replaced with a new one within 6 months. For print quality, a variable amount of ink remains in the cartridge after the “Replace Print Pack” indicator comes on.
For more information see the
PictureMate Show User's Guide
.

faqs.question: How long should an ink cartridge remain in my product if it's not used often?
faqs.answer: When an installed ink cartridge is more than six months old, you may need to replace it if you notice that your printouts don't look as good as they used to and quality doesn't improve after cleaning and aligning the print head.

faqs.question: Which photo cartridge should I use with my product?
faqs.answer: Use the initial photo cartridge included with your PictureMate first. Then use the photo cartridges included with the T5846 or T5845-M Print Packs.

faqs.question: Can the Epson ink cartridges be refilled or can I use third-party ink cartridges without voiding the warranty?
faqs.answer:
Epson does not recommend refilling or using other brands of ink cartridges.  Epson uses a permanent Micro Piezo print head that has allowed Epson to lead the industry in delivering consistent photo image quality by using variable-sized droplets.  Micro Piezo print head can also use a wider variety of inks, which has allowed Epson to introduce such ink breakthroughs as DURABrite® and Epson UltraChrome® inks that offer greatly improved humidity resistance, smudge resistance, and fade resistance.
Using refilled ink cartridges will not void the product's original warranty; however, if these products cause a failure, the repair of that failure will not be covered under warranty.

faqs.question: I brought my product with me to a different country and can't find ink for it. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Some Epson printers and ink cartridges are specific to a regional market and not sold worldwide, although the same printers are sold in the U.S. and Canada. If you have a printer sold in the U.S. or Canada, you may not be able to easily get ink cartridges for it in foreign markets.
Unfortunately, because of customs and tax regulations, the Epson E-Stores in the U.S. and Canada are unable to ship to addresses outside the U.S. and Canada.

faqs.question: How do I clean my product?
faqs.answer:
To keep PictureMate working at its best, you should clean it several times a year.
Turn off PictureMate, unplug the power cable, and disconnect the power adapter and any USB cable or device.
Remove all paper, then use a soft brush to clean any dust or dirt from the paper feeder and output tray.
Clean the exterior with a soft, damp cloth.
Use a soft, dry cloth to clean the screen. Do not use liquid or chemical cleaners.
Caution:
Never use a hard or abrasive brush, or alcohol or thinner for cleaning; they can damage the components and case.
Don't get water on the components and don't spray lubricants or oils inside PictureMate.

faqs.question: How do I transfer photos from a memory card to my computer?
faqs.answer:
See
Copy Photos to and From Your Computer
.

faqs.question: Can my product read multiple memory cards at the same time?
faqs.answer: No. Insert just one card at a time.

faqs.question: My memory card is not recognized by my product. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Check the following:
Insert only one card at a time. PictureMate does not read from multiple cards at once.
Make sure you're using a
compatible memory card
.
PictureMate recognizes and can print the first 9,999 photos on a memory card.
Photos must be in JPEG format and taken with a DCF-compliant camera.
PictureMate cannot read progressive-scan JPEG files or RAW files.
Make sure to format your memory card in your camera.
If you access the card from your computer and delete pictures, the card may not work correctly with your camera. Always delete pictures using your camera.
If you copy files from Adobe Photoshop to a memory card, save them as RGB images using the standard save option (non-progressive). Files saved in the CMYK format may not print with the colors you expect.
If you're using Windows XP or XP Professional x64 Edition, you may need to install your Windows storage device driver. See your Windows help for more information.

faqs.question: I deleted some photos from my memory card and now it isn't working in my camera. What should I do?
faqs.answer: If you use your computer to delete pictures from a memory card, the card may not work correctly with your camera. If this happens, back up the memory card pictures to your computer, then use the camera to format the card. Remember to always delete your camera's pictures using your camera, not your computer.

faqs.question: Can my product read the images on my memory card that were saved in Adobe Photoshop?
faqs.answer: Yes, but save them as RGB images using the standard save option (non-progressive). Files saved in the CMYK format may not print with the colors you expect.

faqs.question: Which memory cards are compatible with my product?
faqs.answer:
You can use the following memory cards:
SD (Secure Digital) and SDHC (High Capacity)
miniSD* and miniSDHC*
microSD* and microSDHC*
Sony Memory Stick**
Memory Stick Duo*
Memory Stick Micro*
Memory Stick PRO
Memory Stick PRO Duo*
Memory Stick PRO-HG Duo*
MagicGate Memory Stick**
MagicGate Memory Stick Duo*
Microdrive
CompactFlash (Type I and II)
* Requires adapter. Consult your adapter documentation for any special instructions on using it.
** Maximum capacity 128MB

faqs.question: Can I just pull the memory card out of my product when I'm finished printing?
faqs.answer:
No. Before removing a memory card from the PictureMate, make sure the memory card access light is not flashing. Do not remove a card while the card light is flashing, or you may lose data on the card.
If the PictureMate is connected to your computer, do one of the following before removing the memory card or turning it off:
Windows:
If PictureMate is connected to your computer with a USB cable, right-click the name of your card (removable disk) in My Computer or Windows Explorer, and select
Eject
.
If PictureMate is connected to your computer over a network connection, make sure that the memory card light is not flashing, then remove the card from the slot.
Macintosh:
If PictureMate is connected to your computer with a USB cable, drag the
removable disk icon from your desktop into the trash.
If PictureMate is connected to your computer over a network connection, open the hard drive, click the
eject icon for the memory card, then remove the card from the slot.
Caution
: If your Macintosh is connected to the PictureMate over a network, do not drag the Memory Card application icon (see example icon below) to the Trash. If you accidentally delete the icon, you'll need to reinstall it to be able to access memory cards over your network.

faqs.question: What is the largest supported memory card for my product?
faqs.answer:
See our
Maximum Memory Card Specifications
page for the specifications.

faqs.question: Can I read or write to my memory card when my product display indicates that one or more ink cartridges are expended?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can read or write to a memory card when the installed ink cartridge is expended. However, you cannot read or write to a memory card if the ink cartridge is not installed.

faqs.question: The paper will not feed correctly. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Check the following:
If paper doesn't feed, remove it, separate the sheets slightly, reload it between the edge guides, and make sure the guides aren't too tight. See
Loading Paper
for more information.
If multiple pages feed at once, remove the paper, separate the sheets, and carefully reload it.
If paper is jams, detach the output tray if necessary and remove the paper. Then press
OK
to clear the jam. Don't pull out jammed paper from the top of PictureMate.
If your paper loads incorrectly or jams frequently:
Use new paper loaded with the glossy or whiter side up, and separate the sheets slightly.
Load a maximum of 20 sheets.
Make sure your paper is beneath the arrow on the edge guides.
Don't load plain paper; this may damage PictureMate.
Use only PictureMate photo paper, or Epson Premium Photo Paper Glossy or Semigloss.
Store paper flat to prevent curling.

faqs.question: Can I print on plain paper with my product?
faqs.answer: No. If you load plain paper, you may damage the PictureMate.

faqs.question: What types of paper can I use with my product?
faqs.answer:
You can use the following types of paper:
Size
4 × 6 inches
Paper types
PictureMate photo paper (included with PictureMate Print Pack)
Epson Premium Photo Paper Glossy
Epson Premium Photo Paper Semi-gloss
Since the quality of any particular brand or type of paper may be changed by the manufacturer at any time, Epson cannot guarantee the quality of any non-Epson brand or type of paper.
Caution:
Don't load plain paper; this may cause damage to PictureMate.

faqs.question: How should I store unused photo paper?
faqs.answer: Store the paper flat to prevent curling, and keep it away from extreme temperatures, high humidity, and bright light.

faqs.question: My product sounds as though it is printing, but nothing prints. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Check the following:
PictureMate may be preparing to print.
The print head may need cleaning. See
Checking and Cleaning the Print Head
.
PictureMate won't operate properly if it's tilted or at an angle. Place it on a flat, stable surface.
Make sure paper is not jammed and is loaded correctly. See
Loading Paper
.

faqs.question: My printout has lines running through it. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following:
The print head may need
cleaning
.
Be sure to print with the glossy or whiter side of the paper face up.
The photo cartridge may need replacing. See
Replacing the Photo Cartridge
.

faqs.question: My printout is blurry or smeared. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Check the following:
Use PictureMate photo paper to ensure proper saturation, absorption of ink, and quality.
Be sure to print with the glossy or whiter side of the paper face up.
The print head may need
cleaning
or
aligning
.
Make sure your paper isn't damp or curled. If it is, load new paper.
Remove each photo from the output tray after printing. Let each photo sit for a minute before handling it.

faqs.question: My printout is grainy when I print from any application. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Check the following:
The print head may need aligning. See
Aligning the Print Head.
Make sure the glossy and whiter side of the paper is face-up.
You may need to increase the image resolution; see your software documentation.

faqs.question: The printout is faint or has gaps. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Check the following:
The print head may need cleaning, see
Checking and Cleaning the Print Head
for instructions.
The photo cartridge may be old or low on ink. See
Replace Print Pack
.
Make sure your paper isn't damaged, old, dirty, or loaded face-down. If it is, load new paper with the glossy or whiter side up.

faqs.question: The colors in my printed photo are wrong or missing. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
The problem could be due to a software setting or the condition of PictureMate. Check the following:
The print head may need cleaning; see
Checking and Cleaning the Print Head
for instructions.
The photo cartridge may be old or ink may be low; see
Replace Print Pack
.
If you're printing from your computer, check your settings; See
Printing From a Windows Computer
or
Printing From a Macintosh
.
Make sure the Color Effect setting is not set to
Black & White
or
Sepia
.
Turn on the
Fix Photo
or
P.I.M.
setting; see
Adjusting Photo Settings
for instructions.
If you copy files from Adobe Photoshop to a memory card, save them as RGB images using the standard save option (non-progressive). Files saved in the CMYK format may not print with the colors you expect.
Colors may change slightly after your print dries. Wait for 24 hours and check your photo again.
Make sure your software is set for color printing.

faqs.question: My product is printing blank pages. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Check the following:
The print head may need cleaning. See
Checking and Cleaning the Print Head
.
The photo cartridge may be old or low. See
Replace Print Pack
to replace it.

faqs.question: Why are the borders or layout incorrect?
faqs.answer:
Try the following:
Select a different Layout setting. If you're printing directly from PictureMate, see
Choosing a Layout
. If you're printing from a computer, see
Printing From a Computer
.
Crop your photo to enlarge and print only a part if it. See
Zooming and Cropping
for instructions.
When you print borderless photos, PictureMate automatically expands your images. If your photos are cut off too much around the edges, you can adjust the amount of expansion. If you're printing directly from PictureMate see
Adjusting Borderless Expansion
. If you're printing from a computer see
Printing From a Computer
.
Your photo size may not match the width/height proportions (aspect ratio) of PictureMate photo paper or the layout you're using. Photos may be cropped to fit the paper and layout. You can use the Crop/Trim Photo(s) feature to size your photo the way you want.

faqs.question: Is there a print test I can run to determine what is causing my print quality problem?
faqs.answer:
Yes. See
Checking and Cleaning the Print Head
to determine if a problem is being caused by your PictureMate or some other source. Try printing another photo to determine if the print quality problem is caused by the image source.

faqs.question: My images saved as CMYK do not look correct. What should I do?
faqs.answer: PictureMate automatically converts RGB images to CMYK. If the image is already CMYK, the color output will not be as expected. Try saving your images as RGB before printing.

faqs.question: My prints have too much magenta in them. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Change the
Color Effect
setting to
None
. The settings you select are applied to all photos you print. They do not change your original image files.
Do the following:
Press the
Menu
button on the remote control.
Select
Adjust Photo Settings
and press
OK
.
Select
Color Effect
and press
OK
.
Select
None
and press
OK
to apply the selected setting.

faqs.question: Why do my prints look blotchy?
faqs.answer:
The prints may look blotchy before they dry completely. Lay them flat and allow them to dry. Do not stack your photos with the printed sides touching.
Note:
Since the quality of any particular brand or type of paper can affect the quality of a print, Epson cannot guarantee the quality of any non-Epson brand or type of paper.

faqs.question: How can I get the latest my product software?
faqs.answer: You can download the latest software from the Downloads for the PictureMate Show.

faqs.question: How can I print wirelessly from a Bluetooth device with my product?
faqs.answer:
See
Printing Wirelessly From a Bluetooth Device
.

faqs.question: Can I connect my digital camera to my product and print directly from the camera?
faqs.answer:
Yes, if your digital camera supports PictBridge printing. For more information, see
Printing From a Digital Camera
.

faqs.question: How do I uninstall my product software?
faqs.answer:
Follow the instructions below for your computer system.
Note:
Do not turn off or disconnect PictureMate while you are uninstalling the software.
Windows
Click
Start
or
, and select
Programs
or
All Programs
.
Select
Epson
or
Epson Printers
, then select
Epson Printer Software Uninstall
.
Note:
With Windows Vista or Windows 7, click
Continue
, then go to the next step.
In the next window, select your Epson PictureMate printer and click
OK
. Then follow the on-screen instructions.
Restart your computer.
Macintosh
Quit all running applications.
Insert the PictureMate CD-ROM into your Macintosh.
Double-click the
Epson
icon.
Unselect all of the items listed, except
Printer Driver
. (Make sure
Printer Driver
stays selected.)
Click
Install
. (If you see a dialog box prompting you to enter your administrator password, enter your password or phrase and click

Note:
The administrator password authenticates or verifies that you are a user with administrator privileges. If you do not know this password, contact the person who administers your computer or Apple for assistance. Epson cannot provide this information to you.
Open the drop-down box in the upper area of the window and select
Uninstall
.
Click
Uninstall
near the bottom-right side of the window.
Follow the on-screen instructions to uninstall the PictureMate software.
After the uninstall, do one of the following:
Mac OS X 10.5 and 10.6
Open
System Preferences
, and select
Print & Fax
. Select your PictureMate model, and click the
-
button.
Mac OS X 10.3 and 10.4
Open the
Applications
folder, open
Utilities
, and select
Printer Setup Utility
. Select your PictureMate model, and click
Delete
.
Restart your Macintosh.

faqs.question: Can my product be networked?
faqs.answer:
Yes. You can set up PictureMate as a shared printer. See
Set Up Network Printing
.

faqs.question: Can I restore my product print settings to their original values?
faqs.answer:
Yes. See
Returning to Default Settings
.

faqs.question: I am having problems installing my product software. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Check the following:
Make sure you follow the instructions for
Installing Software and Connecting PictureMate
in the User's Guide. Don't connect PictureMate to your computer until you are instructed to.
Close other programs, including screen savers and virus protection software, and try installing again.
Make sure your computer meets the
System Requirements
to use PictureMate.
If you're printing over a network, make sure you're computer is configured for shared printing with PictureMate. See
Set Up Network Printing
from instructions.

faqs.question: When I print from Windows 7, the printing time is slow or my product stops printing. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following:
Select a lower quality setting in the printer software.
Make sure your system meets the minimum system requirements for your printer.
Close the
Devices and Printer
in Windows 7 before you print.
Clear space on your hard drive or run a defragmentation utility.
Close programs that you're not using.
Increase your system's memory.

faqs.question: How do I set default print settings when I print from Windows or my Mac?
faqs.answer:
When you change your print settings from within a program, the changes apply only while you're printing at that time in the open program. If you want to select different settings to use in all your programs, you can change the default print settings. Follow the steps below for your operating system to change the default print settings.
Windows 2000, XP, Vista, 7
Right-click the
printer icon in the task bar (bottom-right corner of your screen), and select
Printer Settings
.
If you don't see a
printer icon in the taskbar, do one of the following:
Windows 7
: Click
and select
Devices and Printers
. Right-click the EPSON PictureMate PM 300 and select
Printing Preferences
.
Windows Vista
: Click
, select
Control Panel
, and click
Printer
under
Hardware and Sound
. Right-click the EPSON PictureMate PM 300 and select
Printing Preferences
.
Windows XP
: Click
Start
, select
Control Panel
, then select
Printers and Faxes
(or
Printers and Other Hardware
and then
Printers and Faxes
). Right-click the EPSON PictureMate PM 300 and select
Printing Preferences
.

faqs.answer:

faqs.question: I am unable to connect my product to a wireless network. What should I do?
faqs.answer: The printer does not come with built-in wireless features and does not support a wireless (or Ethernet) connection to a network router. Only a direct wired connection to the computer is supported.

faqs.question: How should I transport my product?
faqs.answer:
See
Take PictureMate With You
.

faqs.question: Nothing happens when I try to print. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
If you're printing from your computer, make sure the USB cable is connected securely at both ends and that the cable meets the
System Requirements
.
If you're printing on a network, see
Set Up Network Printing
for instructions on configuring your PictureMate software for use on a network. If more than one printer driver is installed, make sure the correct driver is selected.

faqs.question: Too many copies are print. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Make sure that the
Copies
option in your software or on PictureMate is set for the number of copies you want to print.

See
PictureMate Print Pack Satisfaction Guarantee

faqs.question: Which battery should I use to replace the battery in the remote control?
faqs.answer: A CR2025 lithium battery.

faqs.question: The product's power will not turn on. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Check the following:
Press the
On
button on PictureMate's side to turn it on. (You can only use the
On
button on the remote control when the power light is orange.)
Make sure the power cable and AC adapter are securely connected at both ends.
Make sure your power outlet works and is not controlled by a wall switch or timer.

faqs.question: How should I store and display my photos?
faqs.answer:
Follow the guidelines below:
Caring for you Photos
To avoid scratches or smudging, do not rub the printed side of the photo.
To prevent smudging, avoid stacking your photos until they are completely dry.
Let photos sit for 24 hours before framing.
After you print, the colors on your photos will take some time to set as the ink dries. During this time, the colors may look different than you expect.
Displaying Your Photos
To ensure photos will last as long as possible, display them under glass or in photo albums.
Keep photos out of the sun to help prevent fading.

faqs.question: How do I back up photos?
faqs.answer:
Before you start, make sure PictureMate is not connected to your computer, then Do the following:
Insert your memory card into PictureMate.
Insert a USB storage device or thumb drive into the
port on the side of PictureMate.
From the Home menu, select
Photo Storage
.
Press
OK
.
Select
Save All Photos
.
Press
OK
, then read the message and press
OK
again.
Follow the instructions on the screen to complete the backup.
If you need to cancel the backup, press
Stop/Clear
.
Caution:
Avoid handling the printer during backup. Also, do not remove the memory card while photos are being saved, or you may lose photos on your card.

faqs.question: The remote control will not turn on my product. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Press the
On
button on the side of the printer to turn on PictureMate (the power light should turn green). The
On
button on the remote control is used to place PictureMate in standby mode to save energy.

faqs.question: My product makes noise after I turn it on or after it has been sitting for a while. What should I do?
faqs.answer: This is normal. It is performing routine maintenance.
